items.speaker: advaita
items.text: O learned one, kindly attend to our proposition.
items.tts: O learned one, kindly attend to our proposition.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: We maintain that this empirical world, whose ultimate status is under dispute, is mithyaa.
items.tts: We maintain that this empirical world, whose ultimate status is under dispute, is ಮಿಥ್ಯಾ.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Our reason is drishyatva: its being an object of cognition.
items.tts: Our reason is ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ: its being an object of cognition.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Consider the silver that appears upon a piece of mother of pearl.
items.tts: Consider the silver that appears upon a piece of mother of pearl.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Although silver is perceived, upon closer examination, we discover that no silver exists there.
items.tts: Although silver is perceived, upon closer examination, we discover that no silver exists there.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Similarly, we propose that whatever is an object of cognition is mithyaa, like the silver appearing in mother of pearl.
items.tts: Similarly, we propose that whatever is an object of cognition is ಮಿಥ್ಯಾ, like the silver appearing in mother of pearl.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: This world, too, is an object of cognition.
items.tts: This world, too, is an object of cognition.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Therefore, we conclude that the world is mithyaa.
items.tts: Therefore, we conclude that the world is ಮಿಥ್ಯಾ.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Just as the appearance of silver is negated by correct knowledge of the shell, the claim that the world possesses ultimate, independent reality must also be subjected to examination.
items.tts: Just as the appearance of silver is negated by correct knowledge of the shell, the claim that the world possesses ultimate, independent reality must also be subjected to examination.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: One moment, venerable scholar!
items.tts: One moment, venerable scholar!

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Before accepting your conclusion, we must first examine the precise nature of what you seek to establish.
items.tts: Before accepting your conclusion, we must first examine the precise nature of what you seek to establish.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: What exactly do you mean by mithyaatva?
items.tts: What exactly do you mean by ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: If you mean absolute non-existence, how do you account for the silver that is actually experienced upon the mother of pearl?
items.tts: If you mean absolute non-existence, how do you account for the silver that is actually experienced upon the mother of pearl?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: But if you define it as sadasad-vilakshanatva, that which is distinct from both ultimate existence and absolute non-existence, then another difficulty arises.
items.tts: But if you define it as ಸದಸದ್ವಿಲಕ್ಷಣತ್ವ, that which is distinct from both ultimate existence and absolute non-existence, then another difficulty arises.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: What precisely constitutes existence?
items.tts: What precisely constitutes existence?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: And what constitutes non-existence?
items.tts: And what constitutes non-existence?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: How can the absence of existence, and the absence of non-existence, seemingly opposed to one another, reside in the same locus?
items.tts: How can the absence of existence, and the absence of non-existence, seemingly opposed to one another, reside in the same locus?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Until the definition itself is established without contradiction, how can the conclusion resting upon it be accepted?
items.tts: Until the definition itself is established without contradiction, how can the conclusion resting upon it be accepted?

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: An excellent question, learned one!
items.tts: An excellent question, learned one!

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: We do not maintain that the world is utterly non-existent, like the horn of a hare.
items.tts: We do not maintain that the world is utterly non-existent, like the horn of a hare.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: By existence, we mean trikaala-abaadhyatva: that which remains unsublated throughout the three periods of time.
items.tts: By existence, we mean ತ್ರಿಕಾಲಾಬಾಧ್ಯತ್ವ: that which remains unsublated throughout the three periods of time.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Past, present, and future.
items.tts: Past, present, and future.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: By absolute non-existence, we mean that which is incapable of ever appearing as existent, in any locus.
items.tts: By absolute non-existence, we mean that which is incapable of ever appearing as existent, in any locus.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Consider again the silver perceived upon mother of pearl.
items.tts: Consider again the silver perceived upon mother of pearl.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: It appears to consciousness.
items.tts: It appears to consciousness.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Yet, when correct knowledge arises, that appearance is sublated.
items.tts: Yet, when correct knowledge arises, that appearance is sublated.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Thus, it is neither ultimately real, like Brahman, nor utterly incapable of appearance, like a hare’s horn.
items.tts: Thus, it is neither ultimately real, like ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನ್, nor utterly incapable of appearance, like a hare’s horn.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: This is what we mean by sadasad-vilakshanatva.
items.tts: This is what we mean by ಸದಸದ್ವಿಲಕ್ಷಣತ್ವ.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: And now, let us turn to the testimony of the Chhaandogya Upanishad.
items.tts: And now, let us turn to the testimony of the ಛಾಂದೋಗ್ಯ ಉಪನಿಷತ್.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Sad eva somya, idam agra aaseet, ekam eva adviteeyam.
items.tts: ಸದೇವ ಸೋಮ್ಯೇದಮಗ್ರ ಆಸೀದೇಕಮೇವಾದ್ವಿತೀಯಮ್.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: In the beginning, dear one, this was Being alone, one without a second.
items.tts: In the beginning, dear one, this was Being alone, one without a second.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: And elsewhere, the same scripture declares.
items.tts: And elsewhere, the same scripture declares.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Vaachaarambhanam vikaaro naamadheyam, mrittiketyeva satyam.
items.tts: ವಾಚಾರಮ್ಭಣಂ ವಿಕಾರೋ ನಾಮಧೇಯಂ ಮೃತ್ತಿಕೇತ್ಯೇವ ಸತ್ಯಮ್.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: A modification is merely a name arising through speech; clay alone is real.
items.tts: A modification is merely a name arising through speech; clay alone is real.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Reflect upon this carefully, venerable scholar.
items.tts: Reflect upon this carefully, venerable scholar.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: A pot possesses a distinct name and form.
items.tts: A pot possesses a distinct name and form.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Yet, without clay, where is the pot?
items.tts: Yet, without clay, where is the pot?

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Its apparent individuality depends entirely upon its underlying material reality.
items.tts: Its apparent individuality depends entirely upon its underlying material reality.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Likewise, we maintain that this universe of names and forms possesses no independent ultimate existence apart from Brahman.
items.tts: Likewise, we maintain that this universe of names and forms possesses no independent ultimate existence apart from ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನ್.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: And it is precisely here, respected scholar, that our inquiry must deepen!
items.tts: And it is precisely here, respected scholar, that our inquiry must deepen!

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: We readily acknowledge that the pot depends upon clay.
items.tts: We readily acknowledge that the pot depends upon clay.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: But from where does it follow, that dependence necessarily implies mithyaatva?
items.tts: But from where does it follow, that dependence necessarily implies ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: A pot can hold water.
items.tts: A pot can hold water.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: An unshaped lump of clay cannot perform that function in the same manner.
items.tts: An unshaped lump of clay cannot perform that function in the same manner.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: The distinctive properties of the pot are established through direct perception.
items.tts: The distinctive properties of the pot are established through direct perception.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Therefore, the dependence of an object upon its cause, does not, by itself, establish that the object is unreal.
items.tts: Therefore, the dependence of an object upon its cause, does not, by itself, establish that the object is unreal.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Consider also your example of the silver appearing upon mother of pearl.
items.tts: Consider also your example of the silver appearing upon mother of pearl.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: In that case, a correcting cognition arises: This is not silver.
items.tts: In that case, a correcting cognition arises: This is not silver.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Thus, the mistaken appearance is demonstrably sublated.
items.tts: Thus, the mistaken appearance is demonstrably sublated.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: But in the case of this waking world, what corresponding valid means of knowledge establishes its sublation?
items.tts: But in the case of this waking world, what corresponding valid means of knowledge establishes its sublation?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Furthermore, consider the declaration of the Katha Upanishad.
items.tts: Furthermore, consider the declaration of the ಕಠ ಉಪನಿಷತ್.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Eko bahoonaam, yo vidadhaati kaamaan.
items.tts: ಏಕೋ ಬಹೂನಾಂ ಯೋ ವಿದಧಾತಿ ಕಾಮಾನ್.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: The One who fulfills the desires of the many.
items.tts: The One who fulfills the desires of the many.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Here, the relationship between the One and the many is expressed.
items.tts: Here, the relationship between the One and the many is expressed.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: The intended meaning of this distinction must also be examined.
items.tts: The intended meaning of this distinction must also be examined.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Dependence upon another does not, by itself, establish the non-reality of that which depends.
items.tts: Dependence upon another does not, by itself, establish the non-reality of that which depends.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Your question is reasonable.
items.tts: Your question is reasonable.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: We do not deny that a pot possesses the capacity to hold water.
items.tts: We do not deny that a pot possesses the capacity to hold water.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Indeed, we fully acknowledge vyaavahaarika sattaa: reality at the level of ordinary experience and practical activity.
items.tts: Indeed, we fully acknowledge ವ್ಯಾವಹಾರಿಕ ಸತ್ತಾ: reality at the level of ordinary experience and practical activity.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Yet, the successful functioning of an object within experience does not, by itself, establish its paaramaarthika sattaa: ultimate reality.
items.tts: Yet, the successful functioning of an object within experience does not, by itself, establish its ಪಾರಮಾರ್ಥಿಕ ಸತ್ತಾ: ultimate reality.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Consider the experience of a dream.
items.tts: Consider the experience of a dream.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Within the dream, pleasure, suffering, movement, and countless other experiences appear meaningful.
items.tts: Within the dream, pleasure, suffering, movement, and countless other experiences appear meaningful.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Yet, upon awakening, the dream world is sublated.
items.tts: Yet, upon awakening, the dream world is sublated.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: Through this example, we demonstrate only that practical experience does not automatically establish ultimate reality.
items.tts: Through this example, we demonstrate only that practical experience does not automatically establish ultimate reality.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: We do not claim that the waking world and the dream world are identical in every respect.
items.tts: We do not claim that the waking world and the dream world are identical in every respect.

items.speaker: advaita
items.text: According to our position, the ultimate sublation of the empirical world is accomplished through knowledge of Brahman.
items.tts: According to our position, the ultimate sublation of the empirical world is accomplished through knowledge of ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನ್.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Then let us return to the very foundation of your inference.
items.tts: Then let us return to the very foundation of your inference.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: You have declared: Because it possesses drishyatva.
items.tts: You have declared: Because it possesses ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: But what precisely is the definition of drishyatva?
items.tts: But what precisely is the definition of ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Do you mean vritti-vyaapyatva: being encompassed by a cognition’s mental modification?
items.tts: Do you mean ವೃತ್ತಿವ್ಯಾಪ್ಯತ್ವ: being encompassed by a cognition’s mental modification?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Or phala-vyaapyatva: being encompassed by the resulting manifestation of knowledge?
items.tts: Or ಫಲವ್ಯಾಪ್ಯತ್ವ: being encompassed by the resulting manifestation of knowledge?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Or perhaps asva-prakaashatva: not being self-luminous?
items.tts: Or perhaps ಅಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶತ್ವ: not being self-luminous?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: In the example of the silver appearing upon mother of pearl, its sublation is established.
items.tts: In the example of the silver appearing upon mother of pearl, its sublation is established.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: But by what valid means of knowledge have you established an invariable relationship between drishyatva and mithyaatva, throughout the entire empirical world?
items.tts: But by what valid means of knowledge have you established an invariable relationship between ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ and ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ, throughout the entire empirical world?

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: One example alone does not establish vyaapti: an invariable relation between the reason, and what is to be proved.
items.tts: One example alone does not establish ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ: an invariable relation between the reason, and what is to be proved.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: Therefore, the fundamental question remains.
items.tts: Therefore, the fundamental question remains.

items.speaker: dvaita
items.text: How can drishyatva be established as an avyabhichaari linga, an unfailing logical indicator, of mithyaatva?
items.tts: How can ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ be established as an ಅವ್ಯಭಿಚಾರಿ ಲಿಂಗ, an unfailing logical indicator, of ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ?

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: Thus concludes the first dialogue.
items.tts: Thus concludes the first dialogue.

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: The definition of mithyaatva has been examined.
items.tts: The definition of ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ has been examined.

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: The examples have been presented, and questioned.
items.tts: The examples have been presented, and questioned.

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: Yet the question of vyaapti remains unresolved.
items.tts: Yet the question of ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ remains unresolved.

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: In our next dialogue, we shall examine whether drishyatva truly constitutes a valid reason for establishing mithyaatva.
items.tts: In our next dialogue, we shall examine whether ದೃಶ್ಯತ್ವ truly constitutes a valid reason for establishing ಮಿಥ್ಯಾತ್ವ.

items.speaker: moderator
items.text: Until then, let the inquiry into truth continue.
items.tts: Until then, let the inquiry into truth continue.
